claim: The retrieved digitization of the Corpus of Indus Seals and Inscriptions contains 179 artefact files, 179 object records and 179 distinct object identifiers, every one of them carrying the side suffix A.
locator: mayig/indus-valley-script-corpus @ ad2f1e2, corpus/m001_m099/ and corpus/m100_m199/; counted by 04-AUDITS/domain-k-indus-corpus.py
notes: One side per object. No object in the file set records a reverse, a boss, an edge or a second inscribed face, so nothing here bears on multi-sided objects.

claim: Every object in the retrieved digitization is a Mohenjo-daro object in the CISI M-series, numbered M-1 to M-184 with five numbers absent: 2, 11, 76, 156 and 168.
locator: same, object id field of every record; 04-AUDITS/domain-k-indus-corpus.py
notes: One site. Nothing in the file set is from Harappa, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan, Chanhu-daro, Gonur, Ur or any other findspot, so no distributional statement about the Indus script can be made from it.

claim: All 179 records carry one of five descriptions, and all five are unicorn seals: unicorn IV 96, unicorn III 45, unicorn II 19, unicorn V 10, unicorn I 9.
locator: same, description field; 04-AUDITS/domain-k-indus-corpus.py
notes: This is the single most limiting fact about the only Indus dataset reachable in this session. It is not a sample of the corpus. It is one iconographic class of stamp seal at one site. No sealing, tablet, pot graffito, copper plate, bangle, ivory rod or inscribed tool is in it, so the object-class distribution that every functional argument depends on cannot be measured here at all.

claim: The 179 records carry 1,003 graphemes, of which 19 are the digitization's damage placeholder, leaving 984 sign tokens. Counting signs only, inscription length runs from 1 to 13, mean 5.50, median 5; counting every grapheme, mean 5.60.
locator: same, graphemes arrays; 04-AUDITS/domain-k-indus-corpus.py; full length histogram in the method note
notes: A measurement of unicorn seals at Mohenjo-daro as one annotator transcribed them, not of Indus inscriptions in general. Longer inscriptions on other object classes are excluded by DK-M-003, so this distribution is truncated by construction and must not be quoted as the length distribution of the script. The two means are given because a reader counting the file naively gets 1,003 and 5.60; see DK-M-025.

claim: The 984 sign tokens realise 181 distinct sign classes, of which 77 occur exactly once: 42.5% of the classes present, 7.8% of the tokens.

claim: The bundled sign list folds 662 Parpola V-numbers into 396 sign classes: 201 classes take one V-number, 195 take more than one, the largest takes 7, and one class takes none.

notes: The allography decision - which shapes are variants of one sign - is what turns 662 forms into 397 classes. It is an analyst's decision, and this one is a single annotator's, following Parpola's most inclusive scheme as he read it (DEP-030).
